children: Gold futures trade lower but remain within the $4,300-$4,400 range, as rising U.S. Treasury yields and a rebound in crude prices weigh on the precious metal. Traders are also assessing the Federal Reserve's interest-rate outlook following last week's hike, as persistent inflation risks could require additional tightening. "This week's calendar is relatively light," analysts at Sucden Financial say. "However, Fed speakers could still add macro noise and skew flows, particularly around the future path of interest rates," they add. But "even if a more dovish tone comes through from officials, markets may be reluctant to price it in fully." In early European trading, New York gold futures fall 0.6% to $4,356.20 a troy ounce. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
